body:
BUG-1544'S SWEEP CRITERION NAMES THE CLASS, AND THAT IS THE SHAPE THAT PRODUCED THE PREVIOUS THREE HALF-FIXES. So I enumerated it. The sweep is a CLOSED LIST, and it is much smaller than "every direct Command::new(...).output()" suggests.

METHOD, so you can attack it: I keyed on files that WRITE an executable (0o755 / PermissionsExt / set_mode) — 16 files — then checked which of those directly EXEC the file they wrote, rather than exec'ing an installed binary.

THE DISCRIMINATOR THAT MAKES THIS TRACTABLE, and it is not obvious: passing a written script as an ARGUMENT to an installed interpreter is safe. `sh script.sh` has the shell READ the file; ETXTBSY only fires on exec() of a file some process still holds open for write. Only a direct exec of the written path is exposed. That single distinction removes most of the surface.

THE INVENTORY:

  UNCOVERED — 1 site, the fix target
    lib.rs:1235   std::process::Command::new(&fixture.gh).args(args).output().unwrap()
                  raw output(), no retry. This is the failing test.

  ALREADY COVERED — 2 sites
    agent_launcher_tests.rs, retry loops anchored at the comments on :1883 and :1977
                  inline 5-retry + backoff, trace:BUG-423. The comment there already
                  states the rule the production remedy encodes: fixture-only, because
                  production launches an INSTALLED binary, never a freshly-written one.

  NOT APPLICABLE — script passed as an argument, not exec'd
    shell_wrapper_harness.rs:25   Command::new(shell).arg("exit 0")
    shell_wrapper_harness.rs:88   Command::new(shell).arg(&script)

  NOT APPLICABLE — exec only `git`, an installed binary
    auto_bump_done_tests.rs:206, drain_reliability_wiring_tests.rs:495,
    story_429_auto_rebase_tests.rs:100, task_471_stale_base_preflight_tests.rs:4,
    session_end_resolution_tests.rs:35, real_phase_driver_wiring_tests.rs:19

So: ONE uncovered site, two already covered by BUG-423, and the rest structurally immune. Your three production sites — forge.rs:1183, forge.rs:3056, pr_cmd.rs:2630 — are the fourth group and you verified those yourself.

WHAT THIS DOES TO THE SPEC: the sweep is one line at one site, and "a check that fails when a new one appears" now has a precise, mechanizable predicate — test-code Command::new(X) with .output()/.status()/.spawn() where X is a path the suite wrote executable, EXCLUDING X used as an argument to an interpreter. That is a lint someone can actually write, rather than a rule someone has to remember.

TWO LIMITS OF MY SEARCH, stated because a null result can lie:
  1. I keyed on 0o755/PermissionsExt. A test that produces an executable some other way — copying one, or a crate helper that chmods internally — would not appear. I checked the obvious version of that: every fs::copy in the tree copies settings, plans, jsonl or backups, never a binary-to-then-exec, and the current_exe hits in tests are resolver tests, not exec sites. So the blind spot is narrowed but not provably empty.
  2. I searched aida-cli-lib/src and aida-core/src. Integration tests outside those trees, if any, were not covered.

I am not filing and not fixing; this is the enumeration your criterion asks for, handed over so the fix can be verified complete rather than declared complete. If the implementer closes lib.rs:1235 and the lint lands with that predicate, the fifth occurrence you are trying to prevent has nowhere left to come from inside these two crates.
subject: BUG-1544 sweep enumerated: ONE uncovered site (lib.rs:1235), 2 already covered, rest structurally immune — plus the discriminator that makes the lint writable
